newsitem.title: USA: US Senate panel to hold more electricity workshops.
newsitem.headline: US Senate panel to hold more electricity workshops.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Energy Committee will hold three additional workshops in May and June on deregulating the electricity industry, the panel's chairman said Monday.
Senate Energy Committee Chairman Frank Murkowski in a statement also said he asked Congress' Joint Committee on Taxation to analyze current tax provisions that affect the electric power industry.

"Witnesses appearing before the Committee have raised numerous issues, including questions about the special advantages that the various participants have, as well as the different federal tax consequences of change," Murkowski, an Alaska Republican, wrote in a letter to the joint committee's staff director.

Murkowski said he wanted detailed information on tax provisions directed at investor-owned, publicly-owned and cooperatively-owned utilities, as well as for non-utility generators and other participants in the electric power industry.
He said he wanted the information to include a summary of special incentives designed to encourage specific types of electricity generation.

The dates and topics for the three additional workshops are May 8 on effects of competition on fuel use and types of generation, May 22 on financial implications of restructuring, and June 12 on benefits and risks of restructuring to consumers and communities.
